title: 第3章 父与子
slug: 帝国的崛起全本免费-帝国的崛起最新章节列表
content_zh:
中年的王储轻轻的翻了几页后并没有回答，而是看了看立在旁边的宫廷总管谢林伯爵。后者负责巴伐利亚王室主要的日常工作，不仅仅对内，还有对外。
“海军方面对新式装甲非常满意，并且表示愿意订购。从目前来看，老侯爵对海外扩张也持支持的态度，海军的建设已经提到了议事日程之上。而目前，帝国内部只有我们可以生产这种装甲，我们没有赔钱的可能。”谢林伯爵的几句话简明扼要的说明了现在的情况。
虽然巴伐利亚一般不会对帝国的大政方针产生影响，但是对于帝国内部的一举一动还是知晓的。在十九世纪九十年代即将来临的时候，在德国国内工业已经日趋饱和需要更多的市场和原料产地的时候，向外扩张成了历史的必然，千万不要只以为就熊孩子威廉二世是个要“争夺阳光下的地图”的德国领导人。铁血首相俾斯麦也是这样一个人，而且他获得的更多而遭到的反击却很少，这就是手段和技术问题了，从这个角度来看说威廉二世是个熊孩子一点都不错，好处没捞到多少，仇家结了一箩筐！要知道，德国在非洲的殖民地几乎都是俾斯麦时代拿到的，威廉二世咋呼了半天，捞到什么好处？
而既然殖民地有了，而且还和某些国家有争端（比如说和美国在萨摩亚的争端），而原有的战舰又不堪用的情况下，那么造新船就成了必然！和某些造船穿越者不同的是，现在的局面对于鲁普雷希特来说无论如何都是赚的，毕竟海军部可能会出现有眼不识泰山的情况，但是无论你造什么船都需要装甲钢啊！在没有分号的情况下，你告诉我，你能怎么选择？
“很好，具体的事情你的手下和谢林伯爵交流一下就可以了，涉及到资金的问题，你可以和皇室金库总管霍亨斯坦因伯爵联系。海军方面我会找人打招呼的。”两人的说辞打消了王储殿下最后一丝顾虑，这个事就这么定了，原则上同意，至于怎么干，你自己看着办。
“你这件事情做的很好，不过我希望你还是能以一个统治者而不是一个资本家的眼光来看待这个国家，我们需要从全局来看如何改变这个国家，你的另一份计划我已经看过了，但是我并不专业，需要有专业的人来和你探讨。我今天想和你说的另外一个问题就是巴伐利亚在未来的帝国乃至整个中欧的地位问题，我想听听你的意见。”王储合上手边的文件问道。
“中欧的桥梁，德意志帝国和奥匈帝国联接的纽带。”鲁普雷希特的回答非常简单，也非常现实！这是目前最符合巴伐利亚国情的决定。先把经济和交通搞好，其它的以后再说。政治和外交是不能随便表态的，或者换句话说，面对实力强过自己太多的普鲁士，巴伐利亚能活到现在，那完全是见风使舵的结果。在这一点上，鲁普雷希特也不得不给自己的先王们点个赞！
要知道，当初德意志统一之前的时候，王国和公国可不仅仅是现在这几家，普奥战争爆发后，普鲁士不但把奥匈排挤出去，同时还把汉诺威王国和黑森公国等一批小诸侯全部吃掉了，而巴伐利亚为何能幸免呢？因为当初人家没有履行和奥地利之间的义务，没有提供多大帮助。所以在战争结束后，没有被老威廉和首相秋后算帐，而且也因为巴伐利亚确实有点力量，所以保持了相对独立的地位，外加相当多的政府拨款来换取巴伐利亚的支持。
而现在，奥匈帝国需要依靠德国的力量和俄国争夺巴尔干地区，几乎可以称得上是德国的小弟了，巴伐利亚这时候再跳腾那不是自讨没趣？而且从目前的情况来看，待遇还不错，没事闹腾什么
“巴伐利亚虽然在矿产资源上十分贫瘠，但是却位于德奥的中心！境内同时又大量的河流经过，如果发展内河航运的话对于巴伐利亚的经济和地位提升有很大的帮助。在保证和普鲁士有良好关系的同时，我们也应该适当加强和奥匈帝国的联系，毕竟双方无论是从历史传承还是血缘上来说都是很密切的，我们有必要维持下去。”鲁普雷希特说道。

content_en:
The middle-aged crown prince turned a few pages gently and did not answer. Instead, he looked at the palace steward, Earl Schelling, who was standing next to him. The latter is responsible for the main daily work of the Bavarian royal family, not only internally, but also externally.
"The Navy is very satisfied with the new armor and expressed its willingness to order it. Judging from the current situation, the old Marquis also supports overseas expansion, and the construction of the Navy has been put on the agenda. At present, we are the only one in the empire who can produce this kind of armor, and we have no possibility of losing money." A few words from Count Schelling succinctly explained the current situation.
Although Bavaria generally does not have an impact on the empire's major policies, it is still aware of every move within the empire. As the 1890s are approaching, when Germany's domestic industry has become increasingly saturated and requires more markets and sources of raw materials, outward expansion has become a historical necessity. Don't just think that the naughty Wilhelm II is a German leader who wants to "compete for the map under the sun." The iron-blooded Prime Minister Bismarck was also such a person, and he gained more but received very little counterattack. This was a matter of means and technology. From this point of view, it is not bad at all to say that Wilhelm II was a naughty child, but he did not gain much benefit, and his enemies were full of enemies! You know, almost all of Germany's colonies in Africa were acquired during the Bismarck era. Wilhelm II kept fussing for a long time, but what benefits did he gain?
And now that there are colonies, and there are disputes with certain countries (such as the dispute with the United States in Samoa), and the original warships are unusable, then building new ships has become inevitable! Unlike some shipbuilding time travelers, the current situation is profitable for Ruprecht no matter what. After all, the Admiralty may be blind to sight, but no matter what ship you build, you need armored steel! In the absence of a semicolon, tell me, what are your options?
"Very good. For specific matters, your subordinates can just communicate with Count Schelling. If it involves funds, you can contact Count Hohenstein, the head of the royal treasury. I will find someone to say hello to the navy." The words of the two people dispelled the last concern of His Royal Highness the Crown Prince. The matter has been settled. In principle, it is agreed. As for what to do, it is up to you.
"You have done a good job, but I hope you can still look at this country from the perspective of a ruler rather than a capitalist. We need to look at how to change this country from an overall perspective. I have already read your other plan, but I am not professional and need a professional to discuss it with you. Another issue I want to talk to you about today is the status of Bavaria in the future empire and even Central Europe. I want to hear your opinion." The crown prince closed the document at hand and asked.
"The bridge between Central Europe and the link between the German Empire and the Austro-Hungarian Empire." Ruprecht's answer was very simple and very realistic! This is the decision that is most in line with Bavaria's national conditions at present. Let’s do a good job in economy and transportation first, and we’ll talk about the rest later. Politics and diplomacy cannot be expressed casually, or in other words, facing Prussia, which is much stronger than itself, Bavaria can survive until now, which is entirely the result of adapting to the wind. At this point, Ruprecht also had to give a thumbs up to his ancestors!
You know, before the unification of Germany, there were more than just these kingdoms and principalities. After the Austro-Prussian War broke out, Prussia not only squeezed out Austria-Hungary, but also ate up a group of small princes such as the Kingdom of Hanover and the Duchy of Hesse. Why was Bavaria spared? Because they did not fulfill their obligations with Austria and did not provide much help. Therefore, after the war, there was no reckoning between old William and the Prime Minister, and also because BavariaIt does have some power, so it maintains a relatively independent position, plus considerable government funding in exchange for Bavaria's support.
Now, the Austro-Hungarian Empire needs to rely on the power of Germany to compete with Russia for the Balkans. It can almost be called Germany's younger brother. Isn't Bavaria asking for trouble if it jumps around at this time? And judging from the current situation, the treatment is pretty good, so there’s nothing to make a fuss about.
"Although Bavaria is very poor in mineral resources, it is located in the center of Germany and Austria! At the same time, a large number of rivers pass through the territory. If inland shipping is developed, it will be of great help to Bavaria's economy and status. While ensuring a good relationship with Prussia, we should also appropriately strengthen our ties with the Austro-Hungarian Empire. After all, the two sides are very close in terms of historical inheritance and blood, and we need to maintain it." Ruprecht said.
